newsitem.title: USA: Cusiana crude trades at WTI minus $1.42 a barrel.
newsitem.headline: Cusiana crude trades at WTI minus $1.42 a barrel.

text.p: A European equity producer sold a cargo of Cusiana crude oil to a U.S. refiner for a discount of $1.42 a barrel to West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, down seven cents from the last confirmed deal, trade sources said Wednesday.
The 550,000 barrel cargo loads June 30 to July 1, the sources said.
Hefty Caribbean freight rates weighed down the latest price, even though a tight transatlantic arbitrage has restricted supplies of competing Brent cargoes in the U.S. Gulf, according to the sources.
Meanwhile, Colombian state oil company Ecopetrol is seeking bids for two Cusiana cargoes loading July 6-10 and July 15-19, sources said.
Cusiana production, currently around 185,000 barrels per day (bpd), is set to rise to between 250,000 and 300,000 bpd withing the next two months.
About seven cargoes of Cusiana now load each month. --Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
